options.action: Use a separately authorized disposable resource experiment with the unchanged expanded dataset, arrivals, deadlines, ranking and freshness checks. Measure CPU and worker lanes together before selecting any hosted tier.

assumptions: The sampled near-two-core saturation is the limiting resource.
Throughput scales perfectly with additional CPU and enough independent workers.
No additional read, write, memory, I/O or provider overhead appears.

constraints: Increasing schedules alone cannot remove saturated database work.
A four-lane worker pool can become the next concurrency limit.
Keep per-lane non-overlap, connection caps, query deadlines and bounded history cleanup.
No hosted resource purchase, quota change or scheduler activation is authorized by this proposal.

options.action: Reduce repeated per-viewer catalog authorization and ranking through a reviewed statement-scoped batch authorization path or exact shared candidate index with revision-based invalidation and conservative bounds.
acceptance: Preserve every canonical top-200 ID and key, including affinity, following, seen and author-diversity effects.
Retain incoming block, private, hidden, deletion and session checks under current authority and recheck at hydration.
Invalidate for post, score, graph, privacy and preference changes before reusing cross-statement work.
Retain the canonical fallback whenever an exact proof is unavailable.
Demonstrate at least the measured 3.2-fold preparation-rate gap under the original 2-CPU/2-GiB profile before hosted QA.

releaseSequence: Preserve the original deployed scheduler and existing release behavior while the expanded gate is blocked.
Rerun both exact-source native profiles after a material query/architecture change, or report a separate resource-profile result without relabeling the original failure.
After isolated acceptance, perform the read-only QA preflight, a bounded actual-scheduler canary, and verify rollback.
Apply reviewed query and scheduler changes only after the selected profile, budget and release gates are authorized.
